newsitem.title: JAPAN: SOCCER-BISMARCK LEADS KASHIMA BACK TO HEAD OF TABLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BISMARCK LEADS KASHIMA BACK TO HEAD OF TABLE.

text.p: Brazilian midfielder Bismarck scored two goals and set up two others on Saturday to help Kashima thrash Kyoto 4-0 at home and reclaim the J-League lead.

The sure-footed Bismarck easily put away goals in the 14th and 80th minutes on a rain-soaked pitch as the Antlers overhauled idle Kashiwa to go one point clear atop the 17-club table with seven rounds left.

Brazilian Mazinho and defender Yutaka Akita, helped by leadup work from Bimarck, scored the other goals for the defending league champions, who retook the lead they gave up with a shock 4-0 loss to Kashiwa on May 3.
Japanese international midfielder Motohiro Yamaguchi headed home a last-minute winner, his first goal of the season, to give the Yokohama Flugels a 2-1 victory over Gamba Osaka at Toyama.
The loss dimmed Gamba's title hopes already suffering under tight marking against high-scoring Cameroon forward Patrick Mboma.
Yokohama Marinos won 3-1 at bottom-placed Fukuoka thanks to two late goals by Spain's World Cup star Julio Salinas, whose injury has limited him to only four league appearances so far.

Dutchman Peter Bosz blasted home a sudden-death goal to earn Ichihara two points with a 3-2 extra time win over lowly host Vissel Kobe, while Australian international Graham Arnold's goal led Shimizu to a 1-0 win at Matsuyama in a battle of mid-table sides.
